article_title: Assessment of Knowledge of Acute Kidney Injury among Non-Nephrology Doctors in Two Government Hospitals in Ondo City, Southwest, Nigeria.
citation: Adejumo Oluseyi, Akinbodewa Ayodeji, Alli Oladimeji, Olufemi Pirisola, Olatunji Abolarin. (2017). Assessment of Knowledge of Acute Kidney Injury among Non-Nephrology Doctors in Two Government Hospitals in Ondo City, Southwest, Nigeria. Ethiopian Journal of Health Sciences. https://doi.org/10.4314/ejhs.v27i2.7
title: 32-item validated AKI knowledge questionnaire with scoring bands
description: A closed-ended structured questionnaire of 32 questions assessing AKI knowledge across clinical features, types, risk factors, nephrotoxic medications, diagnosis and staging criteria, newer biomarkers and renal replacement therapy indications. It was piloted with 20 non-nephrology doctors at State Specialist Hospital Akure, and "The Cronbach's alpha internal consistency coefficient of the questionnaire was 0.72". Each correct answer scores 1 point (maximum 32), with 24–32 good, 16–23 fair and <16 poor knowledge.
requirements: Administered as a self-administered pretested questionnaire to non-nephrology doctors; scoring uses the printed 24–32 / 16–23 / <16 bands
constraints: The instrument was validated in a pilot with 20 respondents in a different hospital and the authors note the main study's small sample limits generalisability
target_learning_goals: assessing knowledge of acute kidney injury prevention, diagnosis and management
examples: Used in the Ondo City cross-sectional survey of 81 doctors between April and May 2016 with a 90% response rate
